findings.description: The code opens a file with inFile.open(argv[1]); but does not check if the file was successfully opened.
Using while (!inFile.eof()) is a common C++ anti-pattern. The EOF flag is only set after a failed read, so you may process an empty or invalid string at the end.
The code assumes all words in the word bank and user input are of the same length, but does not check this.
The global variable deadEnds is declared but unused. While not a direct vulnerability, global variables can lead to maintainability and thread-safety issues.
The main loop in main() could potentially loop forever if the ladder cannot be found and ladder.size() never changes.
No validation on user input for word and target.
